title: A Unified GF(4)–Symplectic Framework for Quantum Error Correction: Constructive Derivation of the Steane [[7,1,3]] Code and Pedagogical Foundation for Modern Codes
content: Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computation, yet its presentation often fragments into disjoint mathematical formalisms—group theory for Pauli algebras, finite-field arithmetic for code construction, symplectic geometry for commutativity, and circuit design for fault-tolerant implementation. This fragmentation obscures the elegant algebraic unity that makes stabilizer codes both theoretically profound and practically implementable.We present a complete, constructive derivation of the Steane [[7,1,3]] code within a unified framework that seamlessly integrates GF(4) algebra, binary symplectic representation, and stabilizer formalism. Starting from the classical Hamming [7,4,3] code, we demonstrate: (1) how GF(4) naturally encodes the Pauli group modulo phases, (2) how the symplectic inner product on F22nF22n​ captures quantum commutation via matrix multiplication, (3) how syndrome extraction reduces to binary linear algebra, and (4) how transversal Clifford gates emerge from symplectic transformations. The derivation encompasses stabilizer construction, centralizer analysis, logical operator identification, distance verification, and fault-tolerant syndrome measurement via flagged circuits—all derived using elementary finite-field arithmetic and binary linear algebra.Beyond the Steane code, we show how this framework extends systematically to subsystem codes and quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, illustrating its versatility for modern code design. This work serves both as a pedagogical tutorial for students entering quantum error correction and as a unified reference for researchers implementing stabilizer codes in practice, bridging the gap between abstract mathematics and hardware implementation.
